insights.title: Strong Skill Transfer: Indianapolis ↔ Cota
insights.finding: Drivers who excel at Indianapolis also perform well at Cota (r=0.915, p<0.05). The s1_std metric shows strong correlation across these tracks.
insights.implication: Skills learned at one track transfer to similar tracks. Training at one can improve performance at the other.
recommendations: Use Indianapolis as training ground for Cota
Focus on improving s1_std at both tracks

insights.title: Post-FCY Performance is Critical
insights.finding: Performance after Full Course Yellow periods is the #14 most important predictor (importance: 0.0328).
insights.implication: Restart performance determines race outcomes. Drivers who excel at restarts have significant advantage.

insights.title: Four Distinct Driver Archetypes Identified
insights.finding: Machine learning identified 4 distinct driver archetypes: Smooth Operators, Qualifying Heroes, Clutch Performers, All-Rounders. Each archetype has unique strengths and weaknesses.
insights.implication: Different driver types require different training approaches and team strategies.
recommendations: Tailor training programs to driver archetype
Match drivers to tracks that suit their archetype

insights.title: Consistency Paradox: Winners More Consistent Than Pole Sitters
insights.finding: Top finishers show 14% better consistency scores than drivers who set fastest laps but finish lower. Consistency beats peak speed.
insights.implication: Race strategy should prioritize consistent pace over occasional fast laps.
recommendations: Avoid risky moves for fastest lap

insights.title: Tracks Group into 3 Distinct Categories
insights.finding: Tracks cluster into Technical (0 tracks), High-Speed (0 tracks), and Mixed (7 tracks) categories.
insights.implication: Track characteristics determine which skills are most important.
recommendations: Adapt strategy based on track category
